# THE TABLES CONFORMANCE MANIFEST (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3, §7, §16, §19).
#
# The registry every language driver reads. It is DATA: a port implements the
# driver contract in test/conformance/README.md, points it at this file, and
# the harness is the gate. Nothing here names a language.
#
# Line kinds:
#
#   unit     <key> <schema path>...
#            a compilation unit, by the key the other lines use.
#
#   instance <name> <unit> <root> <wire file>
#            one table instance, in TWO forms that must agree: the table wire
#            bytes at <wire file> (§3) and the JSON text at
#            testdata/conformance/tables/json/<name>.json (§16). The same
#            instance both ways.
#
#   retain   <case> <unit> <root> <wire> <capacity> <ids> <counters> <save lost> <save>
#            one RETAIN-UNKNOWN round trip (§6.6): the wire, the two capacities
#            the caller declares, the counters the LOAD owes and the one the
#            SAVE adds, and the file the pair writes back. The byte capacity is
#            a RULE where a number would not travel, a record's byte cost is
#            the port's own, so `full` and `short` say what a leg DOES rather
#            than how many bytes it declares, and the id list, being a COUNT,
#            travels as one. Retention is the variable form's alone: the
#            message form is fixed tables only (§3.3).
#
#   report   <case> <unit> <root> <wire file>
#            bytes read by a type that did not write them — the evolution class
#            (§4). The counters are the whole expectation, and they live in
#            reports.txt keyed by <case>, because they are GENERATED and this
#            file is hand-authored.
#
#   cook     <case> <unit> <root> <dump file>
#            a cooked file (§7) — materialised by test/cookgen, which is
#            deterministic — and the canonical node dump its Open must produce,
#            byte for byte. <case> names the FIXTURE and <root> the table it is
#            opened at: one root can have more than one fixture.
#
#   block    <name> <unit> <block file>
#            a block image (§19) an Open must accept.
#
#   forgery  <name> <kind> <subject> <base> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#            one damaged fixture and the verdict every implementation owes it.
#            A forgery is a PATCH over a base fixture, because a patch is what a
#            person can review; the harness materialises the file, and a driver
#            only ever meets a path and the extent its caller claims.
#
# Wire files are REFERENCED where they already live rather than copied: the
# table-wire goldens are the same files test/tables/main.cpp pins.

# Required-construct witnesses are populated and pinned by the generated Go
# runtime. They are ordinary instances, so every native language driver must
# read and write the same canonical bytes; no feature-only side pass can win.
unit featurewitnesses testdata/conformance/feature-witnesses/full/Features.schema
instance feature_full featurewitnesses Root testdata/conformance/feature-witnesses/full/Root.bin
instance feature_array_root featurewitnesses ArrayRoot testdata/conformance/feature-witnesses/full/ArrayRoot.bin

unit tabledemo tables/examples
unit tblv1     test/tables/V1.schema
unit tblv2     test/tables/V2.schema
unit tblp1     test/tables/P1.schema

unit tblp2     test/tables/P2.schema

unit blockdemo tables/block
unit messagedemo tables/messages
unit streamdemo tables/stream
unit blobdemo  tables/blobs

# pins gate 1 for all nine targets and eight of them refuse wide text on either
# wire (SPEC.md §4.12). A leg without the construct answers ABSENT here.

# THE VARIABLE CLASS (§3.1), and the four shapes the numbering has to get right.
# Three carry a text (§16.7): a tree reads and writes as nested tables, and
# graph_shared is the one a tree cannot spell — one list node named from `head`,
# from `alias` and from a by-value nesting, and a diamond whose closing
# reference names a node already numbered. Four nodes held by seven slots, the
# shared two under `&node`, and the tool's own cook of these bytes agrees.
#
# graph_deep is `no-text` BY THE FORM'S OWN RULE: a chain nests in the text as
# deep as it is long (§16.7), and 260 nodes is past the depth cap every walk
# carries (§16.2), so the writer refuses it in the reference and in the tool
# alike. It rides the wire, which has no such bound.
instance graph_tree           graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_tree.bin
instance graph_shared         graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_shared.bin
instance graph_empty          graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_empty.bin
instance graph_deep           graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_deep.bin   no-text

# THE MESSAGE CLASS (§2.6): a union whose arms are tables, at three depths in
# messagedemo — ToolBody in the root, EditBody inside a transaction's edits,
# Origin inside an insert. message_ping and message_save pin the rule that a SET
# arm rides even when its body is entirely default, for a type arm and a table
# arm alike; message_empty is the elided None. streamdemo's Frame has a VARIABLE
# arm, so Feed is a region and a root pointer, and its chunk arm's chain is
# numbered through the union. message_batch is the ARRAY OF UNIONS (§3) at the
# same three depths — history counted in the root with a live None slot,
# pending fixed inside the transaction with its None element riding in place,
# origins counted inside the insert.
instance message_open         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_open.bin
instance message_transaction  messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_transaction.bin
instance message_ping         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_ping.bin
instance message_save         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_save.bin
instance message_empty        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_empty.bin
instance message_batch        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_batch.bin
instance message_trace        messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_trace.bin
# THE GENERAL ARMS (§2.6): an arm is a field line, so an arm may be a scalar, a
# string, an enum, a flags mask, a bytes buffer, a bounded array, another union
# or a POINTER. message_arms carries a fixed-array arm in the root body, a flags
# arm and a nested-union arm in the batch; message_arm_edits carries the bounded
# scalar, counted-array, bytes and enum arms inside a transaction's edits;
# message_ack is the PAYLOAD-FREE arm, the arm id with L = 0.
instance message_arms         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_arms.bin
instance message_arm_edits    messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_arm_edits.bin
instance message_ack          messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/conformance/tables/wire/message_ack.bin
instance m1_open              tblm1       Msg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/m1_open.bin
instance m1_save              tblm1       Msg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/m1_save.bin
instance m2_close             tblm2       Msg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/m2_close.bin
instance m2_open              tblm2       Msg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/m2_open.bin
instance stream_chain         streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_chain.bin
instance stream_header        streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_header.bin
instance stream_parts         streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_parts.bin
# THE WALK ORDER (§3.1), told apart: the numbering is ONE declaration-order walk
# that descends a by-value edge IN PLACE, and Feed declares its union arm before
# its pointer fields. Here the arm reaches every node first — frame.chunk.next
# is a, a.next is b, frame.chunk.links names c — and parts names the same three
# in the REVERSE order, [c, b, a], with pair naming b again. The page's walk
# numbers a, b, c as 2, 3, 4; a walk that takes the pointer fields first numbers
# c, b, a as 2, 3, 4 and writes different bytes from the same value. Every other
# seed coincides under both orders, which is exactly what a seed must not rely
# on. The wire is the TOOL's (`schema pack` of the text), and the reference is
# held to it.
instance stream_arm_first     streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_arm_first.bin
# A POINTER ARM IS THE EDGE ITSELF (§2.6, §3.1), in the union field's own
# declaration-order position: the arm names x, parts names y then x again, so
# the walk numbers x, y as 2, 3 and one node is named from an arm and a slot.
instance stream_arm_pointer   streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_arm_pointer.bin
# A UNION ARM NAMED `tag` (tables/stream Frame): the arm's payload is the arm's
# own, and the discriminator beside it is the arm's index. A value
# representation that keys the discriminator and the payload by name in one
# place lets the arm named like the discriminator overwrite it. The wire is the
# TOOL's (`schema pack` of the text), 49 bytes.
instance stream_arm_tag       streamdemo  Feed        testdata/wire/tables/stream_arm_tag.bin

# THE BYTE BUFFER corpus (§2.5): a blob at its used size, pointed at. blob_small
# carries every field once; blob_empty holds a present blob and string of length
# zero beside null slots — two values at the empty end; blob_large is one blob
# past a 64 KiB slab. blob_shared is `no-text` BY THE FORM'S OWN RULE: a blob's
# text is a string, which has no first key to carry `&node`, so a blob two slots
# name has no spelling and the writer refuses the graph (§16.7).
instance blob_small           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_small.bin
instance blob_empty           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_empty.bin
instance blob_large           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_large.bin
# The Go wire writer names its §2.5 refusal for this instance, and so does every
# port refused-by= lists; the reference still writes the bytes (§2.5).
instance blob_shared blobdemo Catalog testdata/wire/tables/blob_shared.bin no-text wire-refused
# THE STRING TERMINATOR, at the two lengths that can see it (§6.3): a *string
# node carries one zero byte after its data, and the node's extent is rounded
# to the arena's alignment like every node's. At a length that is not a
# multiple of eight the rounding absorbs that byte and a region laid out
# without it is byte-identical; at 8 and at 16 it does not, so these two are
# the rows that hold the terminator answerable.
instance blob_str8            blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_str8.bin
instance blob_str16           blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_str16.bin
# BLOB IDENTITY (§2.5, §3.1): a node is numbered by IDENTITY, never by content
# and never per slot. blob_equal_bytes holds two DISTINCT *bytes nodes carrying
# equal bytes — two records that a by-content numbering would merge into one.
# blob_shared_string holds ONE *string node named from two map slots. A blob
# belongs to one slot (§2.5), so every writer refuses it by name: the Go
# writer's MeasureReason names it (go-refusal=), and Lua's Save, Measure and
# message writer answer the same name (refused-by=lua), and so does Lobster's
# Save (refused-by=lobster); a port that names the
# same refusal is counted as that refusal, and every other port is held to the
# committed bytes, as the reference is. Both rows are `no-text`: a blob's text
# is a string with no first key to carry `&node`, so a shared blob has no
# spelling (§16.7).
instance blob_equal_bytes      blobdemo    Catalog     testdata/wire/tables/blob_equal_bytes.bin  no-text
instance blob_shared_string mapdemo Docs testdata/wire/tables/blob_shared_string.bin no-text wire-refused

# WIDE TEXT, kind 33 (§3). wide_empty is the ELISION: wide text takes no
# specified default (SPEC.md §4.12), so an empty wstring writes no line at all.
# wide_sites carries the kind at EVERY site the wire has at once — a table's
# own field, a `type` a table reaches, an element, and a union arm — which is
# what makes it the seed the wire fuzzer plants an ill-formed payload at four
# ways (§4.2). wide_narrow_arm is the same union at its kind 12 arm, so a
# respelling between the two text kinds is an ordinary kind mismatch in both
# directions rather than UTF-8 bytes read as code units.
instance wide_empty           widedemo    Caption     testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_empty.bin
instance wide_title           widedemo    Caption     testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_title.bin
instance wide_sites           widedemo    Caption     testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_sites.bin
instance wide_narrow_arm      widedemo    Caption     testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_narrow_arm.bin
instance wide_stamp           widedemo    Stamp       testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_stamp.bin

# THE EVOLUTION SEAMS (§4): every instance of one generation, read by the
# other. The counters are generated into reports.txt by the Go engine and are
# the expectation every backend must meet.
report v1_cfg_as_v2   tblv2 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v1_cfg.bin
report v1_seams_as_v2 tblv2 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v1_seams.bin
report v2_cfg_as_v1   tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v2_cfg.bin
report v2_seams_as_v1 tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/v2_seams.bin
report p1_as_p3       tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value.bin
report p3_as_p1       tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional.bin
report p1_empty_as_p3 tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value_empty.bin
report p3_empty_as_p1 tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional_empty.bin

# THE FORM BYTE, AND THE REFUSAL ABOVE IT (§3): one row each for form 0, form 6
# and form 0xFF, three bytes no form defines, over a wire that is otherwise
# a good v1 Cfg. Forms 2 and 3 are not among them, because both are forms this
# build carries — the MESSAGE FORM has its own row below (§3.3) and the FIXED
# FORM is §3.4's — and 4 and 5 are RESERVED BY NAME in §3.4's registry, so 6 is
# the first byte that is neither defined nor reserved. A reader that
# meets a byte it does not know refuses by name and NEVER reports damage — the
# refusal moves none of §4's five counters, because nothing was decoded. It is
# why a report carries a VERDICT: a clean read prints the same five zeros.
report form_zero      tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/form_zero.bin
report form_six       tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/form_six.bin
report form_ff        tblv1 Cfg   testdata/wire/tables/form_ff.bin

# AND A REAL MESSAGE READ AS A FILE (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3): the whole of
# one message, handed to a reader that expected a file. A message stored on its
# own is not readable, because its id table is somewhere else, so the read
# REFUSES by name and decodes nothing. The root is any root, because the form
# byte is read FIRST.
report message_as_file tblv1 Cfg  testdata/wire/tables/login_full_message.bin

# THE POINTER SPELLING IS ITS OWN FRAMING (§3.1). T and ?T are wire-identical
# and read each other as instances above; *T rides as a u32 NODE INDEX under
# kind 17 with the body in the node table, so a reader of either other spelling
# meets a kind mismatch and a node table it cannot name. These two are the
# evolution cases that edit says exist, and the counters are the expectation.
report p2_as_p1       tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer.bin
report p2_as_p3       tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer.bin
report p2_empty_as_p1 tblp1 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer_empty.bin
report p2_empty_as_p3 tblp3 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_pointer_empty.bin

# and the VARIABLE reader's own side of the same seam: P2 reads what P1 and P3
# wrote, meets a BODY where it declares an index, and counts it.
report p1_as_p2       tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value.bin
report p3_as_p2       tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_optional.bin
report p1_empty_as_p2 tblp2 Chain testdata/wire/tables/chain_value_empty.bin
# AN ARRAY OF POINTERS read under §3.1's rules, as shared rows: three hand-built
# Feed bodies with one `parts` field each and no node table. The element kind
# 8 where the reader declares 17 is a kind mismatch and the field stays empty;
# five slots against a bound of four keep the prefix and count clamped; a slot
# naming index 7 where no node exists is malformed and discards the whole
# load. The bytes are the reference leg's, built from
# §3's grammar and pinned by test/tables/main.cpp like every other golden.
report parts_elem_kind          streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_elem_kind.bin
report parts_count_past_bound   streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_count_past_bound.bin
report parts_index_out_of_range streamdemo Feed testdata/wire/tables/parts_index_out_of_range.bin
# AN ARRAY OF UNIONS read under §3's rules, as shared rows: two hand-built
# ToolMessage bodies with one `history` field each. The element kind 13 where
# the reader declares 15 is a kind mismatch and the field stays empty —
# `[N]Body` ⇄ `[N]Table` is a reported edit; an arm id no build declares reads
# as a None element, skipped by its length and counted, the slot kept live.
# The bytes are pinned by the C++ leg (test/tables/main.cpp builds them).
report batch_elem_kind   messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/batch_elem_kind.bin
report batch_unknown_arm messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/batch_unknown_arm.bin
# AN OPTIONAL ARRAY read under §2.3's rules, as shared rows: three hand-built
# ToolMessage bodies with one optional-array field each. The element kind 8
# where the reader declares 13 is a kind mismatch and the field reads ABSENT —
# its declared default, exactly as a skipped field's; four elements against a
# bound of three keep the prefix, count clamped, and the field is PRESENT — it
# rode with its own element kind; and a variant id no build names, in the FIXED
# spelling over enums, leaves that slot at None and counts it unknown while the
# field stays present. The bytes are pinned by the C++ leg
# (test/tables/main.cpp builds them).
report trace_elem_kind         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/trace_elem_kind.bin
report trace_count_past_bound  messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/trace_count_past_bound.bin
report marks_unknown_variant   messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/marks_unknown_variant.bin
# the message pair (§2.6, §4): M2 inserted `close` first, removed `save` and
# grew Open, so open's tag moved and both sides meet an arm they cannot name
report m1_open_as_m2  tblm2 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m1_open.bin
report m1_save_as_m2  tblm2 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m1_save.bin
report m2_close_as_m1 tblm1 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m2_close.bin
report m2_open_as_m1  tblm1 Msg testdata/wire/tables/m2_open.bin

# A FIELD THE WRITER DOES NOT WRITE IS NOT AN EDGE (§3.1, schema#440). One
# value with both pointer slots filled: under a FALSE guard the numbering
# visits one of them, so one record rides and the unwritten target takes no
# index; the control is the same value with the guard TRUE, and it writes two.
# A walk that visited every slot would write two both times. Both are `no-text`
# by the form's own rule: a guarded group's untaken side has no text to carry.
instance guard_false_no_edge   tblg1 Guarded testdata/wire/tables/guard_false_no_edge.bin   no-text
instance guard_true_both_edges tblg1 Guarded testdata/wire/tables/guard_true_both_edges.bin no-text
# AND AN ABSENT OPTIONAL'S TABLE IS NOT DESCENDED (§3.1, schema#526). The same
# value one field over: `optional` is `?Wrapped`, a variable-length table, and
# the numbering, the pack measure and the pack gate on the presence companion.
# Absent, a pointer left inside the optional's table costs no record; present,
# the table descends and its pointer is numbered. The absent wire is the
# guard-false wire byte for byte — the added field moved nothing — and the pins
# are the tool's. `no-text`: an absent optional's stale slots have no text.
instance optional_absent_no_edge  tblg1 Guarded testdata/wire/tables/optional_absent_no_edge.bin  no-text
instance optional_present_edge    tblg1 Guarded testdata/wire/tables/optional_present_edge.bin    no-text

# THE ENUM KIND AGAINST THE RAW INTEGER (§3, §4). K2 declares K1's two field
# names with the spellings swapped, so one wire read the other way names both
# directions at once: kind 30 where the reader declares kind 7, and kind 7 where
# it declares kind 30. Two kind mismatches, both fields at their defaults, and
# no raw value ever read as a variant name.
report k1_as_k2  tblk2 Root testdata/wire/tables/k1_as_k2.bin
report k2_as_k1  tblk1 Root testdata/wire/tables/k2_as_k1.bin

# KIND 31 AND KIND 32, AT EVERY POSITION (§3). Where the reader meets them
# decides which event it counts: at a position it CANNOT name the escape is
# skipped by its L and counted unknown, and at a position it DOES name — a
# field, an arm, an array's element kind — it is an ordinary kind mismatch, on
# the rule every other kind already takes. The bytes are the reference leg's,
# built from §3's grammar and pinned by test/tables/main.cpp.
report escape_unnamed_field   messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/escape_unnamed_field.bin
report escape_named_field     messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/escape_named_field.bin
report escape_arm             messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/escape_arm.bin
report escape_element         messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/escape_element.bin
report nopayload_named_field  messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/nopayload_named_field.bin

# BYTES INSIDE AN ENVELOPE ARE SKIPPED (§3, the append rule). A nested-union
# arm whose L runs one byte past the whole inner union it frames: the inner
# union decodes, the byte is stepped over with the arm, the parent reads on,
# and every counter stays zero. Its top-level twin, the same byte after the
# ROOT's terminator, is a stopped read and so not a report row; it rides the
# wire fuzzer's pinned vectors (testdata/wire/tables/fuzz-vectors/INDEX.txt)
# beside this one. The bytes are the reference leg's, pinned by
# test/tables/main.cpp.
report nested_arm_trailing messagedemo ToolMessage testdata/wire/tables/nested_arm_trailing.bin

# THE ARM'S KIND BYTE, at the four pins §3 names. A2 declares `a` as an int64
# arm, `b` as a float32 arm and `c` as a string(8) arm; each row puts a payload
# of another kind under one of those arm ids. The first three are kind
# mismatches with the union None and the siblings intact; the fourth is the
# LENGTH pin — an arm whose L is not its kind's width is that arm's own framing
# damage, malformed, with the parent reading on past L.
report a2_arm_enum_as_int      tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a2_arm_enum_as_int.bin
report a2_arm_pointer_as_int   tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a2_arm_pointer_as_int.bin
report a2_arm_bytes_as_string  tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a2_arm_bytes_as_string.bin
report a2_arm_length_off_width tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a2_arm_length_off_width.bin

# THE ARM EVOLUTION ROWS (§4), each red for one reason. A1 and A2 declare the
# same five arms under the same names at different types, so one wire written
# under A1 and read under A2 names each of the reader's answers to a retyped
# arm exactly once: a width moved UP the signed ladder is WIDENED (§4), the
# arm's payload decoded at its own width and the value the writer's own, with
# the siblings intact; one width and one length (int32 against float32) is a
# kind mismatch with the union None, because the arm header carries the arm's
# kind (§3); a scalar read as a string is a kind mismatch on the same rule;
# four bytes read as a BODY is a kind mismatch with the parent reading on past
# L; and the body arm beside them still round-trips.
report a1_arm_moved_width_as_a2 tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_moved_width.bin
report a1_arm_one_width_as_a2   tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_one_width.bin
report a1_arm_as_string_as_a2   tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_as_string.bin
report a1_arm_as_body_as_a2     tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_as_body.bin
report a1_arm_body_as_a2        tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_body.bin
# and the PAYLOAD-FREE arm A2 does not declare at all: the arm id with L = 0,
# which a reader that cannot name it counts unknown and reads None (§2.6)
report a1_arm_unknown_as_a2     tbla2 Root testdata/wire/tables/a1_arm_unknown.bin

block block_render blockdemo testdata/wire/tables/block_render.bin testdata/conformance/tables/block/block_render.dump
block block_padded blockdemo testdata/wire/tables/block_padded.bin testdata/conformance/tables/block/block_padded.dump

# THE COOKED FILES (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7). The fixture itself is materialised by
# test/cookgen, which is deterministic, so what is pinned here is the canonical
# NODE DUMP: one line per node and one per leaf, the same walk in every
# language, byte-compared. A record laid out one byte differently INSIDE a node
# moves no node offset, so this is the gate the directory check cannot be.
cook Scene       graphdemo Scene    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Scene.dump
cook Depot       graphdemo Depot    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Depot.dump
cook Album       graphdemo Album    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/Album.dump
cook TreeNode    graphdemo TreeNode testdata/conformance/tables/cook/TreeNode.dump
cook ListNode    graphdemo ListNode testdata/conformance/tables/cook/ListNode.dump
# and the VALUED chain, which is why <case> and <root> are two columns: the five
# above are value-initialised, so their dumps lock every offset, every deref and
# every visit order and almost no VALUES. This one carries a value in every
# non-pointer leaf, so the same walk locks what a reader READS as well.
cook SceneValued graphdemo Scene    testdata/conformance/tables/cook/SceneValued.dump

# THE COOK WRITE SIDE (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7.6): a runtime WRITES the cooked
# file and the bytes are `schema cook`'s, byte for byte, in BOTH byte orders.
# Each line names an INSTANCE the file already carries — its unit, root and wire
# are on that line and are not repeated here — and the two files the tool wrote
# from it. `make conformance-generate` writes those; they are generated, like
# the JSON texts and reports.txt, and a byte that MOVES under an unchanged
# schema is stop-the-line.
#
#   cook-write <instance> <little-endian file> <big-endian file>
#
# The big-endian half is not host-dependent: the order is a PARAMETER of the
# write, settled at cook time for the target build (§7), so every leg answers
# both halves on any host.
cook-write root_full              testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_full.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/root_full-be.cook

cook-write archive                testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/archive.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/archive-be.cook
cook-write keyed_config           testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_config.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_config-be.cook
cook-write keyed_default          testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_default.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/keyed_default-be.cook
cook-write v1_cfg                 testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_cfg.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/v1_cfg-be.cook

# THE BLOCK FORGERY BATTERY as data (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §19.2), pinned from
# test/tables/block_main.cpp's eleven by test/conformance/cpp: each row is one
# word of an otherwise valid block image, resolved to a byte offset.
#
#   forgery <name> block <subject> <base> <pointer> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#
# <base> names the block line the image comes from; <extent> is the length the
# CALLER claims (-1: the image's own); <pointer> is the BUFFER the caller holds —
# 0 an aligned base, 1..63 that many bytes past one — because an unaligned base
# is a pointer fact and not a file fact, exactly as in the cook battery below.
# The harness applies the patch and hands a driver a path.
# Repin with: make conformance-pin.
forgery block_magic_foreign        block block_render block_render 0 0x0000 8 0x0                      -1 refuse a foreign magic
forgery block_magic_swapped        block block_render block_render 0 0x0000 8 0x5343484d41424c4b       -1 refuse a block of the other byte order
forgery block_build_version        block block_render block_render 0 0x0008 8 0x863a8eebc1090dc7       -1 refuse a build this one does not match
forgery block_byte_order           block block_render block_render 0 0x0010 8 0x2                      -1 refuse the other byte order in the prologue's own word
forgery block_array_unaligned      block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x141                    -1 refuse an array start not aligned for its element
forgery block_array_in_prologue    block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x0                      -1 refuse an array start inside the projection
forgery block_array_escapes        block block_render block_render 0 0x0030 8 0x783b40                 -1 refuse an array that leaves the block
forgery block_pitch                block block_render block_render 0 0x003c 4 0x60                     -1 refuse a pitch that is not this build's own
forgery block_count_past_extent    block block_render block_render 0 0x0038 4 0xfa0                200000 refuse a count whose rows leave the extent the caller passed
forgery block_count_past_maximum   block block_render block_render 0 0x0038 4 0x1388              7879488 refuse a count past the declared maximum, inside a roomy extent
forgery block_offset_overflow      block block_render block_render 0 0x0020 8 0x7fffffffffffffc0       -1 refuse an offset 64-aligned and just under 2^63 — the forgery fuzzer's find
# THE USED EXTENT'S OWN PADDING (§19.2): the image is untouched and the CALLER's
# bytes stop one short of the rounding the used extent takes to 64. block_render's
# greatest end is 2784 and its file is 2816, so 2815 covers every array and not
# the padding. It is `truncated` rather than `bad_layout` BECAUSE the arrays are
# read first: the used extent is derived from them and has nothing to say until
# they agree.
forgery block_extent_padding       block block_render block_render 0 -1           0     0                            2815 refuse bytes that stop inside the used extent's own padding

# THE BASE'S ALIGNMENT, held by the REFERENCE rather than by a port's own gate
# (§19.2): the image is untouched and the CALLER's buffer sits one byte past an
# aligned base, so the last clause of the read — the one that reads nothing out
# of the block — is the only one that can refuse it. The Elixir lead gate
# (`make tables-elixir-block-lead`) found this arm missing from the battery.
forgery block_base_unaligned       block block_render block_render 1 -1           0     0                             -1 refuse a base one byte past an aligned one

# THE COOK FORGERY BATTERY as data (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §7, §7.4), pinned
# from test/tables/cook_main.cpp's 111 by that binary's emit-forgeries mode:
# every row is one edit to an otherwise valid cook, resolved to byte offsets
# over the fixture test/cookgen writes for this root.
#
#   forgery <name> cook <subject> <base> <pointer> <offset> <width> <value> <extent> <verdict> <label>
#
# <pointer> is the BUFFER the caller holds — 0 an aligned base, 1..63 that
# many bytes past one, `null` no buffer at all — because an unaligned base is
# a pointer fact and not a file fact. <extent> is the length the caller
# claims (-1: the file's own), and a claim SHORT of the file is a truncation.
# The three rows whose verdict is `open` are §7's own ruling written down:
# Open reads the header and points, and those three are cook-check's.
# Repin with: make conformance-pin.

forgery cook_magic_byte3               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4f43b2484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte4               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4f4fbc4d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte5               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4fb0434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte6               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4bb04f434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_byte7               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0xb44f4f434d484353             -1 refuse one byte of the magic
forgery cook_magic_reversed            cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x5343484d434f4f4b             -1 refuse the magic byte-reversed: a cook of the other byte order
forgery cook_magic_block               cook Scene Scene 0    0x0          8     0x4b4c42414d484353             -1 refuse the BLOCK form's magic: a block where a cook was written

# THE HOSTILE-VALUE BATTERY (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.2, §16.3, §17.5): one tree
# per rule the text form states, so a divergence between the compiler's engine
# and a backend shows up as a diff rather than as a happy path that still
# passes. It moved here whole from tables/pack — it was always data, and it had
# a manifest of its own that this file now is.
#
#   json-hostile <case> <unit> <root> <tree> <verdict> [carried-by=<ports> uncarried=<verdict>]
#
# <tree> is the directory `schema pack` reads, so the text is <tree>/<root>.json
# (§17). <verdict> is `refused` or the §4 report the read produces,
# <unknown>,<kind_mismatch>,<widened>,<clamped>,<duplicate>,<malformed>,<verdict>.
#
# A row whose rule was HELD FIRST IN GO (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.3) states the
# standard's <verdict> together with the ports that carry it, `carried-by=<ports>`,
# and the verdict a port that has not taken the rule still gives,
# `uncarried=<verdict>`. The harness expects the standard verdict from a carrying
# port and the uncarried verdict from every other port, and prints the exemption
# by name — it never skips the row. The mark is for reuse: the lone-surrogate
# rows take it as their ports land.
#
# A case that PACKS carries one further invariant, uniform and therefore not
# spelled per row: the bytes it produces load CLEAN in the generated backend —
# report all zero — and re-save byte-identically. That half is
# test/tables/hostile_main.cpp's, which reads these very rows.
json-hostile array-past-bound              tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/array-past-bound   refused
json-hostile base64-empty                  tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/base64-empty       read
json-hostile base64-unpadded               tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/base64-unpadded    read
json-hostile bits-at-max                   tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/bits-at-max        read
json-hostile bits-over-range               tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/bits-over-range    refused
json-hostile bytes-not-base64              tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/bytes-not-base64   refused
json-hostile bytes-overlong                tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/bytes-overlong     refused

# THE NUL ESCAPE INTO BOUNDED TEXT (§16.3): a \u0000 escape that would land
# U+0000 in a bounded string(N) field is refused as text_holds_zero, naming the
# field. A zero in a value the read only SKIPS is not the event, and \u0001
# reads clean. The ports that carry the str-zero-escape rows below carry this
# refusal; every other port stores the zero as text and keeps the counters its
# reader gives until its port.
json-hostile str-zero-byte-bounded         tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/str-zero-byte-bounded refused
json-hostile str-zero-byte-bounded-nested  tabledemo  RootConfig  testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/str-zero-byte-bounded-nested refused
# THE ZERO RULE IN THE TEXT (§16.3): "A JSON string the read would PLACE in text
# storage ... and that decodes to U+0000 ... refuses the read: FromJson returns
# false, the report is Malformed, and Reason reads text_holds_zero:
# <Table>.<field> for the innermost field that held it." A string the read only
# SKIPS — the value of an unknown key — "stores nothing and is not this event".
# Held first in Go, carried by C, C++, Rust, C#, JavaScript, Dart, Java, moo, Lobster, Squirrel, Lua and Luau: the two refusals carry the standard's verdict, and every
# other port keeps the counters its reader gives (it stores the zero as text),
# 0,0,0,0,0,false,read, until its port. The map-key row uses the existing
# `mapdemo` unit's Text root, whose names field is map[string(8)]string(16);
# tabledemo's RootConfig has no string-keyed map.

json-hostile str-zero-escape-map-key       mapdemo    Text        testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/str-zero-escape-map-key refused

# A TEXT LIST'S TOTAL in the text (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §2.13, §16.2), over the
# witness root's `labels [..4]string(8) | total=8`: the read keeps the longest
# prefix whose bytes are within the total and drops the element that would
# carry the sum past it and every element after it, clamped counted ONCE for
# the field. `past` drops "abc" at 9 bytes and the short "a" after it; `at`
# holds exactly 8 bytes and reads clean (feature_full's "é" and "schema" are the
# same boundary as an instance); `after-clamp` clamps its first element at M,
# counted, and then the total drops "a", counted again.

json-hostile text-total-at                 featurewitnesses Root        testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/text-total-at      read
json-hostile text-total-after-clamp        featurewitnesses Root        testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/text-total-after-clamp refused
# A COUNT PAST [..N] AND THE TOTAL, BOTH COUNTED (§2.13): five labels on the
# [..4] list, where "abc" carries the sum to 9 and the total drops it and the
# tail. The fifth element is past the count bound as well, and that clamp is
# counted beside the total's, so the text and the wire (report
# text_total_and_count, the same five labels) both answer two clamps.
json-hostile text-total-and-count          featurewitnesses Root        testdata/conformance/tables/json-hostile/text-total-and-count refused

# THE WIDE SCALARS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3, §16.2): every scalar the type wire
# carries, in a table — the fixed-point family at every width and signedness,
# the 128-bit integers, each as an element and a nested field. The unit is the
# C++ reference's and the tool's; every other leg answers these ABSENT until it
# lands the kinds (§15). scalars2 is the same root as a later build reads it:
# a fixed respelled as an integer and a 128-bit narrowed to 64 (kind
# mismatches), two ranges tightened (clamps on the raw scale), two fields gone.
unit scalars     tables/scalars
unit tblscalars2 test/tables/Scalars2.schema
instance scalars_full    scalars SimState testdata/conformance/tables/wire/scalars_full.bin
instance scalars_default scalars SimState testdata/conformance/tables/wire/scalars_default.bin
instance scalars_edges   scalars SimState testdata/conformance/tables/wire/scalars_edges.bin
report scalars_full_as_2  tblscalars2 SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_full.bin
report scalars_edges_as_2 tblscalars2 SimState testdata/wire/tables/scalars_edges.bin
# a PLAIN TOP-LEVEL SCALAR field, written narrower than the declaration: the
# corpus otherwise pins widening only on arms, list elements and map keys, so
# a later reader that reports those three and misses a field would stay green.
report field_scalar_widen tblscalars2 SimState testdata/wire/tables/field_scalar_widen.bin
cook-write scalars_full    testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_full.cook    testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_full-be.cook
cook-write scalars_default testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_default.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_default-be.cook
cook-write scalars_edges   testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_edges.cook   testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/scalars_edges-be.cook

# the text form's rules at the wide kinds (§16.2): a fixed takes any number
# token whose value is EXACTLY representable in its Q I.F and refuses a finer
# one as the wrong shape, never rounding; out of range clamps on the raw scale;
# a magnitude past 128 bits saturates and counts; a 128-bit integer takes any
# integral token, exact past 2^53

# THE BYTE BUFFER's text rules (§2.5, §16.2): `""` and `null` are two values;

# ---- THE MESSAGE FORM (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3) --------------------------
#
# A FILE carries its own id table and a MESSAGE STREAM announces one and then
# carries none. Two line kinds carry it:
#
#   connection <key> <unit> <build version> <announcement wire file>
#            one CONNECTION's announced table: the unit whose whole vocabulary
#            it carries, the build version that keys it, and the ANNOUNCEMENT
#            itself — an ordinary form 1 file whose trailer IS the table.
#
#   message  <name> <connection> <root> <file-form wire> <message-form wire>
#            one value in BOTH forms. The variable form is an ordinary instance and
#            rides every surface an instance rides; the message form rides the
#            WIRE surface alone, because its text is the file-form vector's byte
#            for byte and a second json/ file would be one golden with two
#            homes. What the pair pins is a ROUND TRIP: loading either form and
#            saving the other reproduces the other's pinned bytes, because the
#            two are two encodings of one value (§3.3). A message-form wire of
#            `-` is a NAMED REFUSAL row: the root is a variable table, the
#            message form is fixed tables only (§3.3), and every leg answers it
#            absent with "variable table: the message form is fixed tables only
#            (SPEC-TABLES §3.3)".
unit backenddemo tables/backend
unit vocabdemo   tables/vocab
unit vocab9demo  tables/vocab9

connection backend_conn backenddemo 0x16d0630a084485ae testdata/wire/tables/backend_conn.bin
connection vocab_conn   vocabdemo   0x40062c876abfc027 testdata/wire/tables/vocab_conn.bin
connection vocab9_conn  vocab9demo  0x3a923c7d0da66dd8 testdata/wire/tables/vocab9_conn.bin
connection graph_conn   graphdemo   0xfdaabe4726d81d5c testdata/wire/tables/graph_conn.bin

# The three backend messages of schema#523, each in both instances: 106 / 273 /
# 104 bytes as files against 52 / 148 / 43 as messages, and 10 / 43 / 10 against
# 3 / 11 / 3 at their declared defaults. A count that moves is a wire that moved.
instance login_full     backenddemo LoginRequest  testdata/conformance/tables/wire/login_full.bin
instance login_default  backenddemo LoginRequest  testdata/conformance/tables/wire/login_default.bin
instance match_full     backenddemo MatchResult   testdata/conformance/tables/wire/match_full.bin
instance match_default  backenddemo MatchResult   testdata/conformance/tables/wire/match_default.bin
instance store_full     backenddemo StorePurchase testdata/conformance/tables/wire/store_full.bin
instance store_default  backenddemo StorePurchase testdata/conformance/tables/wire/store_default.bin

message match_full    backend_conn MatchResult   testdata/conformance/tables/wire/match_full.bin    testdata/wire/tables/match_full_message.bin
message match_default backend_conn MatchResult   testdata/conformance/tables/wire/match_default.bin testdata/wire/tables/match_default_message.bin
message store_full    backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/conformance/tables/wire/store_full.bin    testdata/wire/tables/store_full_message.bin
message store_default backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/conformance/tables/wire/store_default.bin testdata/wire/tables/store_default_message.bin

# THE `was` ROWS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §5, SPEC §4.2). w1_fleet carries string,
# bytes and flags fields OFF their declared defaults beside a node holding every
# default; w1_fleet_default is a fleet of nothing but defaults, which is the
# empty wire, because a string, bytes or flags field at its declared default
# elides as a scalar does. w2_fleet is the same value written by the unit that
# renamed Vessel to Ship under `was`: byte-identical to w1_fleet, type id
# included. The two cross reads are silent, and `make
# tables-was-negative-control` strips the attribute and watches unknown count.
instance w1_fleet             tblw1       Fleet       testdata/wire/tables/w1_fleet.bin
instance w1_fleet_default     tblw1       Fleet       testdata/wire/tables/w1_fleet_default.bin
instance w2_fleet             tblw2       Fleet       testdata/wire/tables/w2_fleet.bin
report w1_fleet_as_w2 tblw2 Fleet testdata/wire/tables/w1_fleet.bin
report w2_fleet_as_w1 tblw1 Fleet testdata/wire/tables/w2_fleet.bin
report w1_fleet_default_as_w2 tblw2 Fleet testdata/wire/tables/w1_fleet_default.bin

# THE VOCABULARY `was` ROWS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §5). r1_cfg holds an enum
# value, a union arm with a payload, a keyed slot and a nested type's field
# whose names R2 renames under `was`: Silver to Argent, ward to shield,
# Buff.multiplier to mult. r1_ping selects the payload-free arm R2 renames
# pong. r2_cfg is r1_cfg's value written by the renamed unit, byte-identical.
# The cross reads are silent, and `make tables-wasrows-negative-control`
# strips the four attributes and watches unknown count.
instance r1_cfg               tblr1       Cfg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/r1_cfg.bin
instance r1_ping              tblr1       Cfg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/r1_ping.bin
instance r2_cfg               tblr2       Cfg         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/r2_cfg.bin
report r1_cfg_as_r2 tblr2 Cfg testdata/wire/tables/r1_cfg.bin
report r1_ping_as_r2 tblr2 Cfg testdata/wire/tables/r1_ping.bin
report r2_cfg_as_r1 tblr1 Cfg testdata/wire/tables/r2_cfg.bin

# THE REASON BESIDE THE NULL (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §6.5, §7, §19.2): one
# TableRefuseReason for a cook's Open, a block's BlockOpen and LoadMeasure's
# -1, the FIRST failing clause in §7's order. Each row names a forgery above
# and the value its refusal must carry, answered on the `cook-reason` and
# `block-reason` surfaces as the enum's own value name. One row per value each
# accelerator can answer, one per clause that shares a value, and two that pin
# the ORDER: a file failing two clauses answers the first.
#
# THE BLOCK'S `truncated` REACHES THIS SURFACE THROUGH THE EXTENT COLUMN, which
# is a caller's length and not a patched word: block_extent_padding leaves the
# image alone and claims one byte less than the used extent's rounding, on the
# precedent cook_claim_one_short set. WHEN IT LANDED IT WAS RED IN FIVE PORTS --
# Rust, C#, Java, JavaScript and Dart -- not because their readers lacked the
# clause but because their drivers raised a claim SHORTER than the image to the
# image's own length, so the input had never been expressible in those five
# (schema#598, and schema#387 is the pointer column's half of that driver work).
# All nine answer `refuse` now. THE BLOCK'S `unaligned_base` IS STILL NOT
# HERE, and that is about the forgery it would need rather than about the
# reason: it is a clause over the ADDRESS the caller passed, and a manifest row
# hands a driver a path rather than a pointer. test/tables/block_main.cpp's
# BlockOpen gate pins all five readings there (a null base, a length under the
# prologue, a length under the arrays, a length inside the padding, an
# unaligned base) beside the match that writes nothing.
#
#   refusal <forgery> <reason>
#

# ---- RETAIN-UNKNOWN (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §6.6) ------------------------------
#
# THE RT SET is the reader and the two newer builds: RT1 cannot name what RT2
# and RT3 wrote, and every row below is one §6.6 owes. The wires are the same
# pinned vectors test/tables/retain_main.cpp writes. Every readable row also
# names the canonical save wire its retained unknowns write back.
#
# `capacity` is `full`, a buffer the whole load fits in, or `short`, ONE BYTE
# SHORT of the last record: a record's byte cost is the port's own, so the
# short row is stated as a rule a leg applies rather than as a number two
# layouts would read differently. `ids` is `full` or the ENTRIES the caller's
# retained-id list holds, which is a COUNT and is comparable.
unit tblrt1 test/tables/RT1.schema
unit tblrt2 test/tables/RT2.schema
unit tblrt3 test/tables/RT3.schema

# THE ROUND TRIP AT DEPTH, and the two capacities. The first save is a pinned
# byte string of its own: moving a field changes the order ids are first used
# in, so the trailer is permuted and every reference moves with it.
retain retain_round_trip   tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt2.bin        full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt1_save.bin
retain retain_truncated    tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt2.bin        short full -
retain retain_ids_short    tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt2.bin        full  2    testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt1_save_id_short.bin

# THE FIVE EXCLUDED CLASSES a wire can carry to the unknown arm, one row each.
# The NODE-INDEX class's row
# is the RECURSIVE shape, which is the widest case it has: an unknown outer
# table holding a nested pointer three bodies down. The SIXTH class, the
# reserved node-table field, has no row, because it is excluded by construction
# and a test cannot reach it.
retain retain_node_index   tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_2.bin full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_2_save.bin
retain retain_enum_variant tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_3.bin full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_3_save.bin
retain retain_union_arm    tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_4.bin full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_4_save.bin
retain retain_keyed_slot   tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_5.bin full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_excluded_5_save.bin
retain retain_node_record  tblrt1 Node testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt3.bin        full  full testdata/wire/tables/retain_rt3_save.bin

# THE COOK'S NODE ALIGNMENT (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §6.2, THE TWO ALIGNMENT
# RULES): a 128-bit list element in holders aligned eight, its own unit so no
# other unit's build version or vocabulary moves. The root's storage is eight
# modulo sixteen, so its extent begins at sizeof rounded to sixteen; an odd
# count of eight-byte tags ends its extent at eight modulo sixteen, so the
# pointed-at holder that follows lands there unless its node aligns to sixteen.
unit widelist tables/widelist
instance widelist_wide widelist Wide testdata/wire/tables/widelist_wide.bin
cook-write widelist_wide testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/widelist_wide.cook testdata/conformance/tables/cook-write/widelist_wide-be.cook

# THE CANONICAL WRITER'S ROWS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.14): each instance is
# built to separate a choice an implementation could make differently, so the
# json-write surface, which compares bytes, goes red on the leg that makes it.
# map_key_order: string, signed and unsigned keys of every map in Fleet given
# out of order — "7" before "10", "-32768" before "-3", "" first, a proper
# prefix before its extension, and "｡" (EF BD A1) before "😀" (F0 9F 98 80),
# the pair UTF-16 code unit order reverses. map_text_order: the same over
# Text's three maps, with every escape class in a key and in a value, base64
# at every padding length and the int32 extremes as keys. feature_key_order:
# the unbounded `map[string]V` key and an optional map, with a pre-epoch
# timestamp one nanosecond before 1970. feature_stamp_frac: a fraction with
# trailing zeros and an offset spelled `+00:00`, which write as `.12` and `Z`.
# text_float32_double_round: the float32 0x15AE43FE and 0x15AE43FD, the only
# positive float32 values whose `%.*g` loop stops at a different precision
# when the read-back is twice rounded (through a double, then narrowed), with
# the integer extremes of ProfileConfig. graph_chain_text: a 128-node chain,
# so its deepest node sits at the depth cap every walk carries (§16.2), indented
# 2 spaces a level, with a shared node defined deep in `head` and referenced
# from `alias`; every reader must take it and every writer must write it.
instance map_key_order             mapdemo           Fleet         testdata/wire/tables/map_key_order.bin
instance map_text_order            mapdemo           Text          testdata/wire/tables/map_text_order.bin
instance feature_key_order         featurewitnesses  Root          testdata/wire/tables/feature_key_order.bin
instance feature_stamp_frac        featurewitnesses  Root          testdata/wire/tables/feature_stamp_frac.bin
instance text_float32_double_round tabledemo         ProfileConfig testdata/conformance/tables/wire/text_float32_double_round.bin
instance graph_chain_text          graphdemo         Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_chain_text.bin

# THE VALUES THE WRITER REFUSES (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.14, W0): json-write
# answers `refused` for each, and a text is a failure. graph_chain_past_cap is
# graph_chain_text one node longer, 129 deep, one past the cap: a wire carries
# it and no writer may (its wire is graph_chain_text.bin decoded by
# internal/tablewire, one ListNode appended to the chain, and encoded again).
# text_refuse_illformed and text_refuse_unpaired hold, in code, what no wire
# and no text can deliver — a narrow field's ill-formed UTF-8
# and a wide field's unpaired surrogate — and the writer refuses rather than
# replacing either with U+FFFD.
json-write-refusal graph_chain_past_cap  graphdemo Scene         testdata/wire/tables/graph_chain_past_cap.bin none
json-write-refusal text_refuse_illformed tabledemo ProfileConfig testdata/conformance/tables/wire/profile_elide.bin       narrow:name
json-write-refusal text_refuse_unpaired  widedemo  Stamp         testdata/conformance/tables/wire/wide_stamp.bin          wide:label

# THE REWRITE ROWS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §22, test/conformance/README.md): every
# corpus input that READS, read by every leg and written back. The canonical

# THE HAND-BUILT NON-CANONICAL SPELLINGS (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §22): each is a
# legal wire no conforming writer produces, so the leg that reads it must write
# the canonical bytes back. Fields out of declaration order with the id table
# no longer in first-use order; and the id table reversed and every reference
# renumbered. A repeated field (rewrite_field_twice.bin) is refused under the
# strict-only read (§3).
rewrite rewrite_fields_reversed tblw1 Fleet testdata/wire/tables/rewrite_fields_reversed.bin
rewrite rewrite_ids_reversed    tblw1 Fleet testdata/wire/tables/rewrite_ids_reversed.bin

# THE WRITE-ALGORITHM EDGES (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §22): one value per degree of
# freedom a writer has, each a trap for one wrong implementation of it. Map keys
# whose byte order and whose UTF-16 or signed order disagree, keys at their
# default (which elide inside the entry), a nested map value that is empty;
# uint16 keys whose little-endian bytes sort the other way; an unbounded string
# key past 127 bytes beside its prefix; a pointer DIAMOND and a list chain the
# depth-first walk numbers before the tree a breadth-first walk would reach
# first; and a union arm that reaches nodes before the pointer fields declared
# after it name them again.
rewrite edge_map_keys      mapdemo          Fleet   testdata/wire/tables/edge_map_keys.bin
rewrite edge_text_keys     mapdemo          Text    testdata/wire/tables/edge_text_keys.bin
rewrite edge_by_name       featurewitnesses Root    testdata/wire/tables/edge_by_name.bin
rewrite edge_graph_diamond graphdemo        Scene   testdata/wire/tables/edge_graph_diamond.bin
rewrite edge_stream_union  streamdemo       Feed    testdata/wire/tables/edge_stream_union.bin
rewrite edge_u64_keys      mapdemo          EdgeRow testdata/wire/tables/edge_u64_keys.bin

# THE WRITE CONTRACT (docs/SPEC.md §5.1): every writer refuses a value its
# declaration does not admit. Each row loads the wire, sets ONE field to the
# value, and saves through the variable-form Save; the verdict is what the save
# owes. Every refused row has a lawful twin at the same boundary that must be
# written, so a driver that refused everything would fail half the battery.
# An assert leg (C, C++, C#, Rust, Java, Dart) answers from its DEBUG build,
# where the check is active; every other leg refuses in every build.
#
#   write-refusal <case> <unit> <root> <wire> <path> <kind> <value> <verdict>
write-refusal wref_range_high      tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     11  refused
write-refusal wref_range_high_ok   tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     10  wrote
write-refusal wref_range_low       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     -1  refused
write-refusal wref_range_low_ok    tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     0   wrote
write-refusal wref_bits_wide       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].channel     int     64  refused
write-refusal wref_bits_wide_ok    tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].channel     int     63  wrote
write-refusal wref_count           tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons                count   9   refused
write-refusal wref_count_ok        tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons                count   8   wrote
write-refusal wref_length          tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           length  17  refused
write-refusal wref_length_ok       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           length  16  wrote
write-refusal wref_enum            tabledemo LoadoutConfig testdata/wire/tables/loadout_full.bin grade                  ordinal 4   refused
write-refusal wref_enum_ok         tabledemo LoadoutConfig testdata/wire/tables/loadout_full.bin grade                  ordinal 3   wrote
write-refusal wref_union_tag       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].effect      tag     3   refused
write-refusal wref_union_tag_ok    tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].effect      tag     2   wrote
write-refusal wref_non_finite      tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].damage      float   nan refused
write-refusal wref_infinite        tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].damage      float   inf refused

# ILL-FORMED TEXT HELD IN STORAGE (docs/SPEC.md §5.1 row 8): what no wire can
# deliver and a program can build. A narrow string holding 61 FF 62 and a wide
# string holding 0061 D800 0062 (a lone high surrogate) are refused, writing
# nothing; the well-formed twins beside them are written. A leg whose string
# type cannot hold the value answers `unrepresentable`; a leg with no wide text
# answers the wide rows absent.
write-refusal wref_text_illformed  tabledemo RootConfig testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin  version_note bytes 61FF62           refused
write-refusal wref_text_wellformed tabledemo RootConfig testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin  version_note bytes 61C3A962         wrote
write-refusal wref_wide_unpaired   widedemo  Caption    testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin title        units 0061D8000062     refused
write-refusal wref_wide_paired     widedemo  Caption    testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin title        units 0061D83DDE000062 wrote
# A zero byte or unit in variable-form text (docs/SPEC.md §5.1 row 8): the
# binary reader calls it ill-formed, so the variable writer refuses it too;
# only the text writer below spells it `\u0000`.
write-refusal wref_text_zero       tabledemo RootConfig testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin  version_note bytes 610062           refused
write-refusal wref_wide_zero       widedemo  Caption    testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin title        units 006100000062     refused

# THE SAME CONTRACT THROUGH THE FIXED FORM'S FixedSave (docs/SPEC.md §5.1): the
# row loads the wire as the variable form does, sets the one field, and saves
# the one value as a fixed batch of one. An assert leg answers from its debug
# build.
write-refusal-fixed fref_range_high      tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     11               refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_range_high_ok   tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].penetration int     10               wrote

write-refusal-fixed fref_bits_wide       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].channel     int     64               refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_bits_wide_ok    tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].channel     int     63               wrote
write-refusal-fixed fref_count           tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons                count   9                refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_count_ok        tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons                count   8                wrote
write-refusal-fixed fref_length          tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           length  17               refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_length_ok       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           length  16               wrote
write-refusal-fixed fref_enum            tabledemo LoadoutConfig testdata/wire/tables/loadout_full.bin grade                  ordinal 4                refused

write-refusal-fixed fref_union_tag       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    weapons[0].effect      tag     3                refused

write-refusal-fixed fref_text_wellformed tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           bytes   61C3A962         wrote
write-refusal-fixed fref_wide_unpaired   widedemo  Caption       testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin   title                  units   0061D8000062     refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_wide_paired     widedemo  Caption       testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin   title                  units   0061D83DDE000062 wrote
# A zero byte or unit in fixed text: the fixed reader refuses it as
# text_ill_formed, so the fixed writer refuses it too and never writes a record
# its own reader would refuse.
write-refusal-fixed fref_text_zero       tabledemo RootConfig    testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin    version_note           bytes   610062           refused
write-refusal-fixed fref_wide_zero       widedemo  Caption       testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin   title                  units   006100000062     refused

# AND THROUGH THE MESSAGE FORM'S SaveMessages (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §3.3, §22.6):
# <unit> is the CONNECTION whose announced vocabulary the batch of one is
# written against. A ranged value off its bounds is refused, never masked,
# wrapped or clamped into the field's width.
write-refusal-message mref_range_high      backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin quantity          int     100      refused
write-refusal-message mref_range_high_ok   backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin quantity          int     99       wrote
write-refusal-message mref_range_low       backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin quantity          int     0        refused
write-refusal-message mref_range_low_ok    backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin quantity          int     1        wrote
write-refusal-message mref_element         backend_conn MatchResult   testdata/wire/tables/match_full.bin players[0].score  int     100001   refused
write-refusal-message mref_element_ok      backend_conn MatchResult   testdata/wire/tables/match_full.bin players[0].score  int     100000   wrote
write-refusal-message mref_length          backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin sku               length  33       refused
write-refusal-message mref_length_ok       backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin sku               length  32       wrote
write-refusal-message mref_enum            backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin currency          ordinal 5        refused
write-refusal-message mref_enum_ok         backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin currency          ordinal 4        wrote
write-refusal-message mref_text_illformed  backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin sku               bytes   61FF62   refused
write-refusal-message mref_text_wellformed backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin sku               bytes   61C3A962 wrote
write-refusal-message mref_text_zero       backend_conn StorePurchase testdata/wire/tables/store_full.bin sku               bytes   610062   refused

# THE TEXT WRITER WRITES A ZERO BYTE OR UNIT (docs/SPEC-TABLES.md §16.3): it
# spells it `\u0000`, it does not refuse it. The driver answers `wrote` when
# the text holds `\u0000` at that field, and `refused` when the writer refused.
write-refusal-json jref_zero_byte tabledemo RootConfig testdata/wire/tables/root_full.bin  version_note bytes 610062       wrote
write-refusal-json jref_zero_unit widedemo  Caption    testdata/wire/tables/wide_title.bin title        units 006100000062 wrote
